bib.title: AUTOPROMPT: Eliciting Knowledge from Language Models with Automatically Generated Prompts

question: Can prompts for masked language models be generated automatically, so that pretrained MLMs can be probed on sentiment, NLI, fact retrieval and relation extraction without manual prompt writing or finetuning?
hypothesis: Automatically searched trigger-token prompts elicit more knowledge from MLMs than manual prompts, and can rival finetuning in low-data settings.
contributions: AUTOPROMPT, a gradient-guided search that builds prompts from shared trigger tokens plus automatically selected label tokens
Evidence that MLMs do sentiment analysis and NLI without finetuning
Better fact retrieval on LAMA than manual and mined prompts
A relation-extraction probe where MLMs beat a supervised RE model, with a perturbed-sentence control

method.summary: Each input is put in a template with a [MASK] slot and a set of trigger tokens shared across all inputs. Trigger tokens start as [MASK] and are updated by a HotFlip-style first-order gradient candidate search, then re-scored by forward passes. Label tokens come from a logistic classifier on the [MASK] embedding projected onto output word embeddings. The MLM is frozen throughout.
method.task: prompt search for MLM probing: sentiment (SST-2), NLI (SICK-E), fact retrieval (LAMA), relation extraction (T-REx)

datasets.name: SICK-E
datasets.split: standard, plus unbiased 2-way and 3-way variants; dev used to choose prompts
datasets.preprocessing: standard set is 56.7% neutral; 2-way and 3-way variants are balanced

datasets.name: T-REx (training facts for AUTOPROMPT)
datasets.size: at most 1000 facts per relation for 41 relations; extra from Wikidata where fewer
datasets.split: 80-20 train/dev for LAMA evaluation; separate 60-20-20 train/dev/test for the T-REx evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: no T-REx triple in the LAMA test set

models.name: Sorokin and Gurevych (2017) RE model
models.init_from: pretrained as in Petroni et al.

inference.decoding: single [MASK] fill; class probability is the sum over label tokens (Eq. 1); for fact retrieval and RE the most likely token
inference.samples: 10 runs on different random data subsets (and seeds for finetuned models) for the low-data experiment; otherwise one prompt search per setting, seeds not stated

parameters.search_iteration: each iteration: top-k candidates from a training batch, scored on a separate batch, best kept; the best prompt on withheld dev data over the whole search is returned
parameters.SST-2 grid: |Vcand| in {10,100}, |Vy| in {1,3,5}, |xtrig| in [3,6]; prompts initialised from the template used to find the label set
parameters.fact retrieval: 5 or 7 trigger tokens; proper nouns and gold objects seen in training excluded from trigger tokens
parameters.label token selection: logistic classifier on [MASK] embedding, then top-k words by s(y,w) (Eqs. 3-5)

other.compute: SST-2 search required 2 days on 8 NVIDIA 2080Ti GPUs (footnote 3)

metrics.name: P@1, P@10, MRR
metrics.definition: rank of the true object in the MLM label-token distribution

baselines: linear probe on average-pooled frozen representations
eval.protocol: best prompt chosen on dev; scores on a withheld test set. RE counts a prediction correct if it matches the canonical object or the surface form in any context sentence.

prompts.purpose: manual SST-2 template (written before automated prompts)

limits: Authors: prompts were near chance on QQP and RTE (preliminary)
Search is greedy over a large discrete space and sometimes brittle
Struggles with imbalanced training data; prompts often just raise the majority label
Only MLMs (BERT-base, RoBERTa-large) tested; autoregressive LMs said to be a trivial extension, not tested
Low-data comparison uses dev-set accuracy, finetuning hyperparameters not given
Search cost: 2 days on 8 2080Ti GPUs for SST-2
Perturbed RE shows much of MLM accuracy comes from stored facts, not extraction
Seeds and batch sizes for the search not stated

terms.definition: tokens shared across all inputs, initialised to [MASK] and updated by the gradient-based search
set V_y of vocabulary tokens whose summed MASK probability gives the class probability
